history.text: Backpropagation is a gradient estimation algorithm used to train artificial neural networks by computing the gradient of the loss function with respect to each weight via the chain rule. It works by propagating the error signal backwards through the network layers, allowing the optimizer to adjust weights to minimise prediction error. Introduced by Rumelhart, Hinton, and Williams in 1986, it remains the foundational training algorithm for deep learning, enabling networks to learn hierarchical feature representations from raw data.

final_answer: Backpropagation is a gradient estimation algorithm used to train artificial neural networks by computing the gradient of the loss function with respect to each weight via the chain rule. It works by propagating the error signal backwards through the network layers, allowing the optimizer to adjust weights to minimise prediction error. Introduced by Rumelhart, Hinton, and Williams in 1986, it remains the foundational training algorithm for deep learning, enabling networks to learn hierarchical feature representations from raw data.
